messages.subject: Re: Standardized Residuals
messages.body_plain:
To clarify, we were wondering if there was a mirt analog to the IRT.residuals() function in TAM, which returns residuals and standardized residuals for each observation in a dataset to which a unidimensional IRT model was applied.

Thank you,
Ray

On Tuesday, October 18, 2022 at 1:23:07 PM UTC-7 Raymond Hernandez wrote:
> Hello,
>
>      Is it possible to get standardized residuals for each item in a scale, for each person? We ran a graded response model in mirt on a 5 item scale. Our understanding was that the "personfit" command computes the average of the standardized residuals across items for each person (e.g. infit/outfit). The "itemfit" command computes the average of standardized residuals for a given item, across all people. Neither though gets at standardized residuals for each item, for each person.
>
>      In case it informs anything, an approach we considered to calculate the standardized residual was following the formula below, where the numerator is the residual and the denominator is the variance of the observed response given theta. We had no problem calculating the residual, but how can we use mirt to calculate the variance of the observed response given theta?
>
>
>
>
>          Thank you,
>
>           Ray
>

messages.subject: Testlet estimated parameters
messages.body_plain:
Dear Phil and community,

I ran the following model testlet model. Output file indicate 90 estimated parameters.
Then, I ran the following bifactor model and output also indicate 90 estimated parameters.

The two model are the same except that the testlet impose a proportionality constraint between the loadings of the general and specific dimensions.

I don't understand why both outputs give the same number of parameters because the testlet model is a constrained version of the bifactor.

Does anyone have an idea ?

Thanks for your help.

Pierre-Charles

#Testlet model

spec1<-c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,3),rep(4,4))
spec2<-'G = 1-15

CONSTRAIN = (1, a1,a2), (2, a1,a2), (3, a1,a2), (4,a1,a2), (5,a1,a2),

CONSTRAIN = (6,a1,a3), (7,a1,a3), (8,a1,a3)

CONSTRAIN = (9,a1,a4), (10,a1,a4), (11,a1,a4)

CONSTRAIN = (12,a1,a5), (13,a1,a5),(14,a1,a5),(15,a1,a5)'

mod.md<-bfactor(ddd, model=spec1, model2 = spec2, SE=TRUE)
mod.md
extract.mirt(mod.md, what="time")
coef(mod.md, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mod.md, printSE=TRUE)
fscores(mod.md, method="EAP", full.scores=T, full.scores.SE <http://full.scores.SE> = TRUE)

#Bifactor model

spec<-c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,3),rep(4,4))

mod.md<-bfactor(ddd, model=spec, SE=T)
mod.md
extract.mirt(mod.md, what='time')
coef(mod.md, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mod.md, printSE=TRUE)
fscores(mod.md, method='EAP', full.scores=T, full.scores.SE <http://full.scores.SE> = TRUE)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have trouble understanding how to do a confirmatory mirt with oblique items. When I do a confirmatory mirt, all factor loadings not specified in the model = 0, and I get very bad results. The model doesn't seem to get any better even if I try to make it as similar as possible to the exploratory mirt results.

Example (not actual results) on what factor loadings look like:
Q1 : 0.678 0.000 0.000 0.000 ...
Q2 : 0.897 0.000 0.000 0.000 ...
Q3: 0.000 0.789 0.000 0.000 ...
....

M2(c_mirt_10_v2, impute=10, QMC = TRUE)
M2 df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95 SRMSR TLI
stats 9020.478 800 0 0.08816329 0.08649754 0.08977199 0.3367542 0.7192893
CFI
stats 0.7348659

My model is something like:
cmodel_10 <- mirt.model('
   F1 = 1,2,3
   F2 = 4,5,6,7,8
   F3 = 9,10,11
   F4 = 12,13,14,15,16,17
   F5 = 18,19,20,21,22,23
   F6 = 24,25,26,27,28
   F7 = 29,30,31,32,33
   F8 = 34,35,36
   F9 = 37,38,39,40,41
   F10 = 42,43,44,45,46,47
   COV = F1*F2*F3*F4*F5*F6*F7*F8*F9*F10')

Do I do something wrong with my confirmatory analysis? Is it normal that the factor loadings is 0.000 for every other factor than the one I specified? Should I instead to a target rotation kinda like
summary(mod1, rotate = 'targetQ', Target = cmodel_10)?
How do I specify the target model when my model is so complex? Do I have to make a binary matrix?

This is my first time doing a confirmatory mirt analysis, so I might have just misunderstood something.

messages.subject: A question on Rasch Vs. 2PL with same a
messages.subject_clean: A question on Rasch Vs. 2PL with same a
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

I have a question on the
difference between Rasch/PCM and 2PL/GPCM that have equal slope parameters. On
page 107 of your latest mirt package document, in the explanation of argument
itemtype, you wrote “'Rasch'
-
Rasch/partial credit model by constraining slopes to 1 and freely estimating
the variance parameters (alternatively, can be specified by applying equality
constraints to the slope parameters in 'gpcm'; Rasch, 1960)”. I don’t think these two
models are the same, as the 2PL/GPCM estimates one more parameter, a1, in
addition to the ones estimated by Rasch/PCM.

Moreover, the anova result of
the Rasch/PCM and 2PL/GPCM is really weird: the df is 0 instead of 1.

For better explanation, please
try the following code:

data <-
expand.table(LSAT7)[1:500,]

mod_rasch <- mirt(data,
itemtype = "Rasch")

mod_equala <- mirt(data,
itemtype = "2PL", constrain = list(seq(1, by=4,
length.out=ncol(data))))

anova(mod_rasch, mod_equala)

Waiting for your reply. Thanks again for developing the mirt
R package.

messages.subject: RMSEA = 0 in M2
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am computing a simple unidimensional graded response model with 7 items (4 levels) and N=98 (I know, that's little). When I calculate the fit indices with M2, I get

            M2 df         p RMSEA RMSEA_5   RMSEA_95     SRMSR      TLI CFI
stats 12.19753 14 0.5904428     0       0 0.08627009 0.0426366 1.003871   1

So, RMSEA is = 0 and CFI, TLI=1 and M2 > df (which is the reason, that RMSEA=0, as I read somewhere).

Is this model feasable to report and calculating factor scores or is there a problem with it, should M2 always be larger than df? I really couldn't find anything in the literature about this case.

I also calculate a CFA with the same model using lavaan and it gave me good fit values, Chi2=16.5, df=14, p=0.28, RMSEA=0.43 [0.00;0.11], SRMR=0.31, CFI=0.999, TLI=0.998.

Thanks a lot for your expertise!

Martin
